claims_disputed.claim: 91.8% of public skills contain at least one detected defect (89.3% violate the official spec), stable at 88.8-94.6% across thresholds.
claims_disputed.reason: Strength is fine, but 'stable' rests only on numeric-threshold variation over a 10,000-skill subsample (§3.3); detector definitions themselves are unvalidated on real skills (no precision audit, §6), so stability is internal to the authors' detector set, not a property of the ecosystem.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The paper never compares progressive disclosure against an alternative. Its only functional evidence is a BM25 Hit@1 gap of 5.9 points (88.5% vs 82.6%, Table 1) with no significance test, and R1-defective includes missing/too-short descriptions (R1.1/R1.2) that mechanically shrink the BM25 index text, so the gap is partly by construction. 'Bloated bodies waste context' is asserted from prior work, not measured here.

missed_issues: Routing stress test (Table 1) has no significance test or CI and does not control for description length; since R1.1/R1.2 defects are defined as missing or <30-char descriptions, lower lexical retrieval is near-tautological.
Platform comparison claim ('Cursor skills are highest quality') covers only the 41.7% of skills attributable by path; the review does not flag that this is conditional (authors admit it in §6).

RQ4 exemplar traits 1, 2, 3, 5 are definitional under the detectors used to select exemplars (authors admit, §4.5); the 'Evidence-Based Authoring Guidelines' framing is partly circular and mildly hype_language/novelty_inflation.
Repair experiment is single_model (GPT-4o-mini) and missing_cost_reporting; the review lists small_sample but not single_model.
note: First review is accurate and well caveated; I'd lower relevance to 3 because skill-file hygiene only informs the team indirectly (no Java, ingestion, multi-repo or SDD evidence), and downgrade the P02 stance because no progressive-disclosure comparison is run.
